blocks.content: Environment variables are a convenient way to pass configuration into a container, but they are a genuinely poor way to pass anything actually sensitive, a database password, an API key. This topic introduces why, the full mechanics live in the Docker Security module.
1. Environment Variables Are Not Actually Hidden
blocks.text: 1. Environment Variables Are Not Actually Hidden

blocks.content: A value passed via -e is easily visible to anyone with access to inspect the container, docker inspect prints it in plain text, as does anything that dumps the container's process environment. "Set as an env var" is not the same thing as "kept secret."

blocks.alt: Anyone who can inspect the container can read it

blocks.content:
docker inspect myapp | grep -A5 '"Env"'
# Shows every environment variable in plain text,
# including anything you meant to keep private.

code.content:
docker inspect myapp | grep -A5 '"Env"'

# including anything you meant to keep private.

codes.bash:
docker inspect myapp | grep -A5 '"Env"'
# Shows every environment variable in plain text,
# including anything you meant to keep private.

blocks.content: Beyond docker inspect, environment variables can leak in other unexpected places too, crash reports that dump the process environment, logging libraries that print configuration on startup, child processes that inherit the full environment by default. A secret in an env var has more exposure surface than it looks like at first glance.

blocks.alt: More exposure surface than it appears to have

blocks.content: Two patterns solve this more properly: mounting a secret as a file instead of an environment variable (readable only by the process, not visible in process listings or inspect output), or reaching for a dedicated secrets manager (HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, or Docker Swarm's own built-in secrets) that hands out short-lived, audited access instead of a static value sitting in configuration.

blocks.alt: File-based secrets and dedicated secret managers, both better

blocks.content: This topic is deliberately a concept-level introduction, the practical mechanics, Docker secrets, mounting secret files correctly, and integrating with a real secrets manager, are covered in complete depth in the Docker Security module.

blocks.alt: The full mechanics are covered in Docker Security

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: A plain environment variable is visible via docker inspect and other tooling, it is convenient, not actually secret.
File-mounted secrets and dedicated secret managers are the properly secure alternatives, covered in full in the Docker Security module.
